findings.headline: Check whether value can be a function; createSignal would run it as a derived signal.
findings.why: value is a parameter typed T, so the caller decides what it holds and it can be a function. Solid 1.x stored a function passed to createSignal as the initial value. Solid 2.0.3 treats createSignal(fn) as a derived signal and calls fn, so the value becomes whatever fn returns.
findings.guidance: If it can hold a function, pass createSignal(() => value): the derived form returns value unchanged whether or not it is a function. Setters have the same rule in both versions: pass setX(() => next) when next can be a function. If it can never be a function, narrow its type so the reader can tell.

findings.headline: Check whether initialValue can be a function; createStore would run it as a derived store.
findings.why: initialValue is what the selector parameter returns, so the caller decides what it holds and it can be a function. Solid 1.x stored a function passed to createStore as the initial value. Solid 2.0.3 treats createStore(fn) as a derived store and calls fn, so the value becomes whatever fn returns.
findings.guidance: A store's initial value must be an object or array. If initialValue can be a function (or a primitive), box it, createStore({ value: initialValue }), or keep it in a signal instead.
